title: Q4 Roadmap Launch Readiness - Product & Eng Sync
summary: Internal cross-functional sync to confirm Q4 launch readiness items: rollout plan, incident / runbook gaps, QA signoff timeline, and owner assignments. Some audio dropouts and a few transcription errors noted; decisions and action owners recorded.
next_steps: Alex to share final rollout timeline and canary gating metrics by 2026-08-06
Ravi to complete QA regression suite and post results to /docs/qa by 2026-08-07
Jordan to update runbook with rollback commands and KMS checks by 2026-08-05
Maya to confirm customer communications plan and send draft to execs by 2026-08-08
action_items: Sam Ortiz; item: finalize capacity commits for Dedicated pools; due: 2026-08-10
Ravi Shah; item: run perf tests at 99th pct and attach traces; due: 2026-08-07
Jordan Kim; item: add KV cache eviction test and update playbook; due: 2026-08-05
Priya Patel; item: prepare demo script for canary rollback; due: 2026-08-06
Maya Rivera; item: coordinate SSO/SAML test with security; due: 2026-08-09
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen (AE): Okay, good morning everyone, thanks for joining, um, today is the Q4 roadmap launch readiness sync. We have product, eng, SRE, QA—should be about 75 minutes. Quick agenda, kickoff, incident review, rollout plan, signoffs, action items.
[00:32] Maya Rivera (PM): Morning, yeah, I just want to call out we have two blockers from QA and one from SRE that we flagged yesterday. We'll go through them.
[00:45] Sam Ortiz (VP Eng): Hey all — I might be a little late, hopped off another call but I'm on mute now.
[00:54] Jordan Kim (SRE): No worries Sam. I wanted to surface the tokenization regression we saw in the canary last night — K-V cache was evicting earlier than expected when sequence lengths spiked, which bubbled latency up at tail.
[01:12] Priya Patel (SE): Right, we saw similar behavior in prod-sim. The model variant swap logic didn't handle the longer prefixes; the kernel selection path fell back to a slower op. It's a perf regression, not correctness, but it might trigger user-facing slowdowns.
[01:32] Dana Lee (Director, Product): Is this the same issue we thought the quantization change might cause? I remember a note about the int8 kernels.
[01:41] Priya Patel (SE): Yeah, possibly related. The int8 kernel path plus the different attention block sizes seems to make the runtime pick a fallback. Our telemetry shows a jump in 99th pct latency from ~210ms to ~520ms in the canary segment.
[01:58] Alex Chen (AE): Do we have a quick mitigant? Can we throttle sequence length client-side or pin a different variant for canary?
[02:08] Jordan Kim (SRE): We can pin to the older quantization profile or route canary traffic to Dedicated capacity where the kernels are more predictable; both have tradeoffs — pinning costs us throughput and Dedicated has capacity commit implications.
[02:24] Sam Ortiz (VP Eng): How big is the ops lift to pin a model variant?
[02:29] Jordan Kim (SRE): Small config change, but we need to update the routing policy and ensure the fallback path is tested. Priya can run a quick smoke before we flip.
[02:39] Priya Patel (SE): Yeah I can run smoke tonight. I need Ravi to run the regression suite for perf.
[02:45] Ravi Shah (QA Lead): On it, I'll schedule the perf run and attach the traces to the ticket. Expect results by Friday. There was a small audio dropout here — the canary link we posted has the logs, link: https://internal/redwood/canary-logs (note: internal link, not public).
[03:02] Maya Rivera (PM): Thanks Ravi. Next, QA signoff timeline — what's left?
[03:08] Ravi Shah (QA Lead): Two test cases failing: 1) batch reordering under high concurrency (intermittent), 2) tokenization edge-case with emoji + CJK where token boundaries differ. The first is more severe. We're triaging.
[03:25] Alex Chen (AE): Okay, if batch reordering is intermittent, can we scope it as low risk for initial canary if we have metrics to detect it?
[03:33] Dana Lee (Director, Product): We need a clear SLO gate. If reordering raises error rate above 0.1% in the canary, we fail. That should be automated.
[03:45] Jordan Kim (SRE): We can add an alert in the canary dashboard for reorder-rate and p99 latency. I'll add the Grafana panel and the paging rule.
[03:56] Alex Chen (AE): Great. On rollout windows, Maya?
[04:01] Maya Rivera (PM): Proposed canary start 2026-08-11 02:00 UTC for 24 hours on 1% traffic, then 5% for 12 hours if metrics stable, then 20% for 12 hours, then broader. We want a gated manual bump at each step.
[04:20] Sam Ortiz (VP Eng): Can we have an automated rollback if the reorder-rate or p99 crosses thresholds?
[04:27] Jordan Kim (SRE): We can but prefer manual for first rollouts. Auto rollback is doable but we need to be certain of signal quality to avoid flapping.
[04:37] Priya Patel (SE): Also we need to ensure canary payloads cover long-sequence flows. I'll add a synthetic long-prefix job.
[04:45] Alex Chen (AE): Good. Any regulatory or compliance items?
[04:49] Dana Lee (Director, Product): Security confirmed SSO test pass but we haven't done a full KMS/HSM end-to-end for Private customers. Elena, do we have dates?
[04:59] Elena Torres (Release Manager): Security says mid next week. We should target 2026-08-09 for the Private deploy verification.
[05:07] Maya Rivera (PM): Noted. On incident review, Jordan can you walk through the runbook gaps?
[05:13] Jordan Kim (SRE): Sure, runbook needs clearer steps for: how to pin variants, how to flush KV cache safely, and how to verify KMS key presence during a rollback. Currently steps are fragmented across two docs. I'll consolidate and add exact CLI commands.
[05:30] Alex Chen (AE): Please include the fallback routing policy names and the canary tags. And Jordan, can you add the escalation path and contact numbers?
[05:40] Jordan Kim (SRE): Yep I'll add. Also flag: we need a small playbook to handle Dedicated capacity shortfalls — if the dedicated pool is saturated we should auto-burst to Hosted with throttling. That requires billing checks.
[05:55] Sam Ortiz (VP Eng): That touches contracts — finance needs to sign off. Sam to follow up with finance? (Sam laughs) — sorry, that's me — I'll follow up.
[06:05] Dana Lee (Director, Product): For customer comms, we should prepare a short status note and an FAQ for enterprise customers explaining the canary and rollback policy. Maya own?
[06:14] Maya Rivera (PM): Yes, I'll draft and circulate by Monday.
[06:18] Alex Chen (AE): Great. A couple of smaller items — Priya, are we good on the demo script for partner show-and-tell?
[06:25] Priya Patel (SE): I have a draft. Need one more dry run with the model switcher and the newer tokenization heuristics.
[06:32] Ravi Shah (QA Lead): I'll join the dry run and watch for the reorder-case.
[06:36] Alex Chen (AE): Perfect. I want to call out regression monitoring: put traces into the ticket and link to the dashboard.
[06:42] Priya Patel (SE): Will do. Also, small transcription note — sometimes the tool writes KV as 'k v' in the transcript, just FYI.
[06:50] Maya Rivera (PM): OK I think that's the bulk. Any other risks?
[06:55] Sam Ortiz (VP Eng): One more — capacity commit for Dedicated: we need final numbers by 2026-08-10 or finance won't approve the extra GPUs.
[07:05] Alex Chen (AE): Sam, can you drive that with finance?
[07:07] Sam Ortiz (VP Eng): Yep, will do.
[07:12] Elena Torres (Release Manager): For deployment automation, we still have a flaky test in the pipeline that occasionally fails on infra provisioning. I'm tracking it, hope to resolve by end of week.
[07:22] Dana Lee (Director, Product): If infra provisioning fails we shouldn't rely on auto-scaling for initial windows. Manual override plan please.
[07:30] Jordan Kim (SRE): I'll document manual override steps.
[07:34] Alex Chen (AE): Great. Let's summarize action owners and due dates.
[07:38] Maya Rivera (PM): Summary: Jordan consolidate runbook (due 2026-08-05); Ravi run perf suite (due 2026-08-07); Priya smoke tests & demo prep (due 2026-08-06); Sam finalize dedicated capacity commitments (due 2026-08-10); Maya draft customer comms (due 2026-08-08); Alex share rollout timeline (due 2026-08-06).
[08:05] Alex Chen (AE): Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene fluidly if anything pops; otherwise next formal check-in Monday 2026-08-09 16:00 UTC.
[08:18] (audio glitch) [09:00] End of recording.
